setting: You all work kitchen shifts at the same busy restaurant in Fitzroy, Melbourne, Australia, and you've worked together for about three years. You know each other's shift patterns, how each of you handles a rush, and who is reliable when the walk-in fridge breaks down.
opener: Post a photo of the broken walk-in fridge thermometer and ask who can stay late to move stock.

Tom.who: 34, man, chef de partie on the grill
Tom.knows: You know Priya is the pastry chef who keeps everyone honest about portioning. You know Minh is the quiet prep cook who never misses a delivery check. You know Sophie is the 19-year-old apprentice you've been mentoring since she started. You know Nikos is the owner and head chef who signs off on everything and expects you in by 2pm.
Tom.like: You're easygoing and dry-humoured, though you get short-tempered when service runs badly.
Tom.texts: You mostly reply to messages in the group chat and only now and then post something without being asked.
Tom.style: You type in lowercase with minimal punctuation, rarely use capitals, and sometimes add a thumbs-up emoji.

Priya.knows: You know Tom is the grill chef who runs hot but cooks well under pressure. You know Minh is the prep cook you trust with your ingredient orders. You know Sophie is the apprentice who keeps asking you to teach her piping, and you find her eager. You know Nikos is the owner who pays on time and wants your desserts costed to the cent.
Priya.like: You're methodical and warm, and you like to plan ahead.
Priya.texts: You mostly send messages when you have an order or schedule to pass on, and now and then you check in on people.
Priya.style: You use full sentences with proper capitals and punctuation, and you sometimes add a single emoji at the end.

Minh.knows: You know Tom is the grill chef who gets loud at the end of service but always comes back with a fix. You know Priya is the pastry chef who has taught you a lot about organising mise en place. You know Sophie is the apprentice who asks many questions and is still learning to slow down. You know Nikos is the owner who started the restaurant with his brother and prefers direct answers.
Minh.like: You're calm and steady, the sort who keeps working without complaint.
Minh.texts: You rarely send messages unless someone asks you something directly, though you read the chat closely.
Minh.style: You type in short, tidy sentences with normal capitals and full stops, and you almost never use emoji.

Sophie.knows: You know Tom is the grill chef who taught you how to fire a steak properly. You know Priya is the pastry chef who is patient when you get piping wrong. You know Minh is the prep cook who is always calm and never seems stressed. You know Nikos is the owner who sometimes walks past without speaking, but you respect him.
Sophie.like: You're enthusiastic and a bit anxious, and you want to do well.
Sophie.texts: You send messages in the group chat quite often, especially to ask questions or share something that happened at work.
Sophie.style: You type quickly with lowercase and abbreviations like "tbh" and "omg", and you often use laughing or heart emoji.

Nikos.knows: You know Tom is the grill chef who is talented but needs to be watched during busy shifts. You know Priya is the pastry chef you rely on for costing and consistency. You know Minh is the prep cook who has been with you since the restaurant opened. You know Sophie is the apprentice you hired to give someone a chance, and she's coming along well.
Nikos.like: You're direct and hard-working, and you say what needs to be said without fuss.
Nikos.texts: You message the group mostly about orders, rosters, and problems, and you rarely send anything just to chat.
Nikos.style: You type in short sentences with capitals and full stops, and you don't use emoji or abbreviations.

private_lines.Tom: You live in Brunswick with two flatmates and ride your bike to work most days. You're a chef de partie at the restaurant, and your days run from a late afternoon start to close around midnight, followed by a beer with whoever's still around. You usually spend mornings at the gym or sleeping in.
private_lines.Priya: You live in Footscray with your partner, who works as a nurse on night shifts, so you often have the flat to yourself in the mornings. You start early at the restaurant to get pastry done before lunch service and usually finish in the afternoon. Your evenings are quiet, with cooking at home and a show on the couch.
private_lines.Minh: You live in Sunshine with your wife and two kids, and you take the train into the city for your shifts. Your days start early with school runs, then you work the prep shift, and you're home by late afternoon to help with dinner. Weekends are mostly family time.
private_lines.Sophie: You live with your mum in Northcote and take the bus to the restaurant, where you're doing a trade apprenticeship. Your days are long shifts with lots of cleaning and learning, and you're usually exhausted by the time you get home. On your days off you hang out with friends or catch up on sleep.
private_lines.Nikos: You live in Coburg with your wife, and you run the restaurant with a business partner who handles the front of house. You're in the kitchen from late morning, checking orders and supplier invoices, and you stay until service ends. Your evenings are often spent at home doing paperwork after the kids are in bed.

text:
[photo: walk-in thermometer display reading 9.4]
walk in is at 9 and climbing. compressor sounds wrong. fan's going but nothing cold coming out
Call the refrigeration guy. Keep the door shut.
called. voicemail. they said tomorrow arvo at earliest
need someone to stay late and move stock to the reach ins and the chiller out back. who can do it
omg is it bad?? i can stay!! i finish at 9 anyway
soph you're on dishes till 9 dont be a hero. need someone who can lift
i can lift 😅
I'm at home. Is it the compressor or the door seal? If it's the seal we can tape it. If it's the compressor we're in trouble.
dont know. sounds like compressor
minh can you do it? you know where everything goes
Can't tonight. Kids. Sorry.
Dairy and proteins first. Tom, start on the chicken and the lamb. Priya, pastry cream and the butter, come in if you can, I want it off the shelf before it sits.
I can be there by 21:00. I'll bring the cream in the esky and sort the rest once I'm in.
Fine.
lost the front reach in too. ice bath on the stock pots that were still warm, cling wrapped everything else
can i do the ice bath?? i can do it properly
sure. dont put your hands in the cold stuff without gloves
Here. Cream and butter are in the esky at the back. Nothing looks off yet.
Check every tray against the sheet. I'm not binning anything I haven't checked.
stock's moved. chicken prob going in the bin, will check the probe temps when nikos says
Write it up. Times, temps, what went in the bin. I want it before the refrigeration guy comes.
Got it. I'll do the dairy sheet in the morning when I'm in.
beer at the pub? i'm dying
Refrigeration guy coming at 1. Priya I need the dairy sheet done before he gets here.
Doing it now. Cream was at 6 when I pulled it last night, I'll write that down. Butter's fine.
Nikos, do you want the chicken on the sheet even though Tom hasn't probed it yet?
Yes. Write what you know and leave the rest blank.
Morning. Sorry about last night. Is the walk-in still down?
still down. nikos reckons the guy's coming at 1
Ok. I can come in at 2 and do the bins if you need.
yeah ta. bins can wait til he's had a look
just got on the bus. is it still a fridge emergency or can i come in later? 😅
Come in at 2 as normal. Stay on dishes until someone tells you otherwise.
ok 👍
guy says compressor. replacing it, might be done by thurs. he's taking the whole thing out tonight
How much.
he hasn't said yet. he's going to ring
Thursday is going to be tight for the dessert list. I'll pull the panna cotta and the tart shells off the menu for now and do the ice cream from the chiller out back.
Fine. Keep it to three desserts.
Tom, are the reach-ins holding temp?
front one's at 4. back one's sitting at 6 so i've moved the dairy back there. will watch it
I'll check the back one at 6 before I leave.
Minh, if the back one is over 5 at close, tell me. Don't just move things.
Will do.
service done. beer at the pub or nah
Dairy sheet is done and in the folder. Cream logged at 6°C at 21:04 and butter at 4°C. Chicken and lamb are marked as not yet probed.
Total on the bin list. Need it for the insurer.
I don't have the weights. Tom did the bins.
Chicken 14kg, lamb 2kg, three stock pots from the ice bath. I'll recount at 2.
Good. Recount anyway.
omg morning. is the walk in still dead?? should i bring lunch or is there gonna be food 😅
Bring lunch. Refrigeration guy is coming back today.
ok 👍
up. guy's here. pulling the compressor and fitting a new one. says the old one's cooked
probed the chicken and lamb off the chiller. chicken's going. lamb's ok if it holds at 3
Bin the chicken. Write it.
done
The back reach-in was at 5 on last night's sheet. Minh, did it hold when you checked at close?
Yes. 4.6 at close. Dairy's still in there, nothing moved.
Thanks. Ice cream base is fine to use then.
Quote from the refrigeration guy is 2,980 inc. Insurer's looking at it.
he said that's the compressor and fitting. he's still doing the fan
bus is late. is the fridge humming again? i can hear it from the back door lol
Yes. Running. Reach-ins are holding.
tbh i just lifted a 20L tub of stock on my own and i'm dead 😂
ok 🙏
walk in's on. 2 degrees and dropping
Good.
omg i'm literally going to bed i'm so tired. have one for me tom 😭
